360 Selections: what “best” means in each context

In merchandise, “best” depends on the objective. These pages organise options from the active catalogue by context and explain the criteria used, without turning a recommendation into a universal promise.
Each selection identifies its criteria, explains the methodology and keeps price, stock and customisation tied to the actual data for each product.
What these pages do not do
They do not invent ratings or reviews.
They do not assign scores without verifiable data.
They do not guarantee future stock or a universal deadline.
They do not replace the final product configuration.

Sustainable merchandise and eco-friendly promotional products
Compare products using available materials, certifications, reusability and environmental data.

Choosing sustainable merchandise should be based on the data available for each product: composition, materials, certifications, reusability and environmental indicators. Not every product provides the same level of information.
The composition and percentage shown on the product help put the use of recycled materials into context.
FSC information identifies products for which the supplier states the use of FSC™-certified materials.
The catalogue may identify products that belong to the supplier’s Our Nature range.
When available, CO₂ is shown in kg of CO₂ equivalent as an additional comparison point.
When available, H₂O adds information about water use associated with the product.
Compare the declared material, composition and product properties. Use terms such as recycled or FSC only when they apply to that specific reference.
Durability, reusability and suitability for the recipient matter too. The product should make sense for its intended use.
Avoid extending environmental claims. Communication should reflect the materials, certifications and indicators actually provided.
Search for recycled, rPET, bamboo, cork or FSC and always confirm the details on the product page.

Understand the factors that affect stock, production, customisation and delivery at 360 Merchandising.
There is no single lead time for the entire catalogue. Availability depends on the product and variant; customised orders can also require artwork preparation, validation, production and shipping.
Stock is specific to each product and variant
Always confirm the final configuration before ordering
Availability is based on synchronised catalogue data. Colours, sizes and other variants within the same product family can have different stock levels.
Lead time can depend on the technique, area, quantity and setup required. Plain and customised products follow different processes.
Some configurations require suitable artwork and approval stages. Supplying correct files early reduces the risk of avoidable delays.
Shipping follows stock allocation and production. Available methods, estimated times and costs are shown during checkout for the relevant order.
For events and fixed deadlines, allow a safety margin and confirm the full lead time before committing to a product.
